text:
Sam W: deploy-bot flagged a blocked promotion to prod. artifacts failing upload and ci jobs keep failing on npm install. anyone looking?

deploy-bot: Promotion blocked -> publishing artifact to s3://redwood-artifacts/prod/ failed with 503 (x3). Holding promotion.

Jess L: seeing repeated extract errors in the CI logs right before upload step. looks like npm tar extraction fails after cache miss. sample:```
npm ERR! tarball data stream error: unexpected end of file
npm WARN tarball tarball data stream error
error An unexpected error occurred: "EPERM: operation not permitted, unlink '/workspace/node_modules/.staging/some-pkg-123'"
```

Kevin H: runner logs show concurrent cache GC on our shared cache host around the same time (gc daemon triggered by ttl sweep). shared cache path is /mnt/runner/cache/npm. TTL is 168h (7d). GC overlapped with CI upload which caused partial artifact to be removed mid-publish.

Maria S: confirmed. S3 multipart uploads show aborted/IncompleteMultipartUpload entries. When runner tries to fetch cached tarball it gets truncated and npm aborts.

Tina (oncall): steps to mitigate? we need to unblock release asap. options: 1) force promote last-good artifact 2) re-run ci with cache disabled to produce fresh artifact 3) extend cache ttl and re-run GC safely.

Sam W: prefer minimal blast radius -> rollback/pin to last good artifact for the release window. what's the last good sha?

deploy-bot: last successful promotion for this release was image ghcr.io/redwood-inference/service-api@sha256:7f4b2c9e and artifact bundle redwood-app-2026-03-18-abc123.tar.gz (sha256:abc123def456).

Kevin H: I can push a manual rollback to canary and then gate prod. command:```
# promote last good artifact
./deploy/promote --env prod --artifact redwood-app-2026-03-18-abc123.tar.gz --force-replace
```
Note: that will skip the new build. We should also disable shared cache GC until we re-run a fresh CI. I'll open a quick infra ticket to pause ttl sweeper.

Jess L: also recommend a short-term CI workaround: run pipeline with `CI_SKIP_CACHE=1` for that commit -> will rebuild node_modules and produce a clean artifact. use:```
CI_SKIP_CACHE=1 ./ci/run_release_pipeline.sh --commit HEAD
```
This takes ~12m longer but avoids the corrupted cache.

Maria S: I'll validate the integrity of the last-good artifact before promote:```
sha256sum redwood-app-2026-03-18-abc123.tar.gz
# expect abc123def456
```

Tina (oncall): I'm going to pause the cache sweeper now and mark the deployment window: change-window until 2026-03-20T10:00Z. Also contacting infra to investigate why GC and uploads overlapped.

Sam W: decision: pin to last-good artifact for immediate unblock, then re-run CI with cache disabled and once we have fresh artifact re-promote. Maria will validate, Kevin will run promote, Jess will kick the rebuild and verify.

Kevin H: on it, running promote now. will update when done.

deploy-bot: Promotion to prod started (manual). replacing artifact with redwood-app-2026-03-18-abc123.tar.gz.

Kevin H: promote completed, health checks passing on 3/3 prod nodes. rolling back the failed release and unlocking the pipeline.

Jess L: kicked the rebuild with `CI_SKIP_CACHE=1`. build succeeded and artifact uploaded fine (no s3 aborts). new artifact sha256: def789abc000.

Maria S: verified last-good artifact sha (abc123def456) and new artifact (def789abc000). both checksums match expectations.

Tina (oncall): leaving cache sweeper paused until infra confirms safe sweep scheduling. will open a follow-up to add a pre-upload lock on cache host to prevent concurrent GC during publish.

Sam W: thanks all. we'll document this in the release notes: revert to pinned artifact to meet SLO, follow up with fix for cache gc/publish coordination and add CI flag to auto-disable cache for critical releases. :thumbsup:

Maria S: filing postmortem draft now and linking logs.

Kevin H: FYI added quick guard to deploy script to retry multipart complete and abort incomplete parts before upload, that'll reduce partial-upload fallout.

Jess L: nice. moving to monitor for any further upload flakiness.

Tina (oncall): closing this thread. reopen if more failures show up. :white_check_mark:
